incidents.victim: ATB Market (Ukraine), Tez Tour and Dodo Pizza (Russia)
incidents.vector: DataSuckers discovered valid credentials in Dodo Pizza's GitHub repositories and used them to access backend systems; the group breached networks, exfiltrated data, destroyed systems, and demanded ransoms.
incidents.impact: Three major organizations breached across the former Soviet states; Russian authorities arrested three of four group members including leader Denis Friedman, who was placed under house arrest and faces up to six years in prison.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders using Ledger hardware wallets
incidents.vector: Ledger hardware wallets sold through authorized resellers in Asia and at MediaMarkt stores across Europe were pre-implanted with covert LTE modules and SIM cards that exfiltrate the device seed phrase upon setup.
incidents.impact: Up to $100 million in cryptocurrency stolen from victims globally; implants confirmed across multiple authorized reseller channels; affected users are advised to immediately move funds off any Ledger device while the supply chain breach is investigated.

incidents.victim: Enterprise organizations using BeyondTrust Remote Support
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-102764, a zero-day file upload vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances, enabling arbitrary PHP webshell deployment and root-level access.
incidents.impact: Attackers harvested credentials from device vaults, established persistent backdoors via webshell and tunneler implants, and pivoted to downstream customer systems via admin session abuse; widespread opportunistic exploitation is expected following public disclosure.

incidents.victim: UK Legal Aid Agency
incidents.vector: Criminals exploited vulnerabilities in the Legal Aid Agency's IT systems to access and exfiltrate personal data; initial disclosure in May 2025 significantly underestimated the scope of the breach.
incidents.impact: Breach now confirmed to include approximately 250,000 records predating 2007 (some from 1978), including criminal histories, probation data, financial assessments, partial payment card details, and the names of judges, lawyers, and civil case parties; stolen data has not yet been published.

incidents.victim: U.S. Federal Bankruptcy Courts (via BAE Systems contractor)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on BAE Systems disrupted the Bankruptcy Noticing Center, the platform BAE operates on behalf of the U.S. federal judiciary to produce and transmit all bankruptcy notices nationwide.
incidents.impact: All federal bankruptcy court noticing systems are unavailable; all production of bankruptcy notices is halted for every federal court across the country; scope of data exposure is unknown.

incidents.victim: Al Jazeera journalists and staff; potentially EU government, NATO and UN personnel, news organizations, and semiconductor manufacturers
incidents.vector: Israeli advertising company Discover-Tech exploited digital ad networks to deliver zero-click Candiru spyware payloads to targeted individuals through standard online advertising, requiring no user interaction.
incidents.impact: Infections confirmed at Al Jazeera headquarters; CitizenLab and Confiant identified ad clusters consistent with targeting of EU governments, NATO and UN networks, global news organizations, and chip manufacturers; Google removed Discover-Tech from its ad platforms and IAB Europe suspended its membership.

incidents.victim: Government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure
incidents.vector: AI-generated PHP and shell script payloads deployed alongside multiple web shells and a Go-based remote access tool with WebSocket C2; targeted Linux servers with modified PHP configurations for persistence, disabling endpoint protection and erasing logs.
incidents.impact: Government mailboxes enumerated to access linked social media accounts; entire database contents exfiltrated; the campaign operated from October 2025 through April 2026 before detection.

incidents.victim: U.S. national security (export control violation)
incidents.vector: Alexander Suvorov operated a Hong Kong front company to illegally procure and export dual-use microelectronics from U.S. companies to Russia, bypassing export controls.
incidents.impact: Russian military obtained dual-use electronic components with applications in radar, precision location, and communications systems; Suvorov extradited from Sweden and faces up to 20 years.

incidents.victim: Telecommunications managed service provider (unnamed)
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2024-47575 in FortiManager to register a rogue device and exfiltrate device configurations, then a FortiOS path traversal vulnerability to deploy a memory-resident ARM64 implant operating entirely within legitimate processes.
incidents.impact: Configurations, credentials, and cryptographic material stolen for 500+ managed FortiGate firewalls protecting both the MSP and its clients; the implant left no persistent binary on disk and was active from September 2024 until disclosed in October 2026.

incidents.victim: Global organizations across 150+ countries (healthcare, financial services, IT sectors)
incidents.vector: Chinese-language criminal marketplace YAM Store sold hijacked Microsoft 365 and Google cloud environments alongside phishing kits impersonating 2,300+ global brands to steal credentials and financial data.
incidents.impact: Over 1 billion phishing messages sent to 75,000+ organizations since January 2026; Microsoft and Health-ISAC obtained a court order, seized infrastructure, disabled 20,000+ accounts, and blocked 100,000+ domains; defendant Yang Jian named.

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Dutch multinational grocery retailer, parent of Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Stop & Shop)
incidents.vector: Unknown attackers compromised IT infrastructure at Ahold Delhaize, one of the world's largest food retail groups, forcing the company to proactively take systems offline across multiple countries.
incidents.impact: Systems taken offline at multiple retail chains across multiple countries; extent of data exposure and full operational impact not yet disclosed.

incidents.victim: French and European grocery retailers
incidents.vector: Unknown attackers exploited unpatched legacy control software in commercial refrigeration systems, abusing the automated defrost function to force continuous heating rather than cooling cycles.
incidents.impact: Refrigeration units in hundreds of French supermarkets heated to 50°C overnight, damaging perishable goods; Australian authorities issued alerts urging OT operators globally to assess their exposure.

incidents.victim: Anywayanyday (Russian online travel agency)
incidents.vector: Unknown attackers compromised the IT infrastructure of Anywayanyday; the attack method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: New flight, train, and hotel bookings suspended; platform website unavailable; all 330,000 hotel and 800 airline partner connections disrupted; no evidence of customer personal data compromise reported.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-104935, a zero-day vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure that grants root-level code execution on fully patched VPN appliances with no user interaction required.
incidents.impact: Actively exploited in limited attacks prior to patch release; CISA added to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; administrators must apply patches immediately and rotate Microsoft Intune credentials if Ivanti Neurons for Intune is in use.

incidents.victim: Government agencies across 9 CIS and Central Asian countries
incidents.vector: Phishing emails with malicious macro-enabled documents, PowerShell downloaders, GitHub-hosted scripts, and a WinRAR exploit; delivered custom reverse shells for persistent access to government networks.
incidents.impact: Government agencies responsible for foreign affairs, economic development, agriculture, and environmental management targeted across Russia, Belarus, Armenia, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, and Azerbaijan; diplomatic communications and strategic resource data sought.

incidents.victim: 70+ U.S. companies (healthcare, communications, retail, manufacturing)
incidents.vector: U.S. facilitators hosted company-issued laptops at residences across Texas, allowing North Korean IT workers to pose as U.S. residents and obtain remote employment using identity theft and wire fraud.
incidents.impact: Approximately $3 million in revenue generated for North Korea from 70+ victimized employers; 14 defendants indicted including Chinese nationals and U.S. citizens, with two arrested; 40 laptop farms disrupted and 187 laptops seized.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (employee data); Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing spin-off)
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft (zero-day first used June 2026), then bypassed WAF rules via URL-encoding to mass-exploit the FBI's HR platform managed by Accenture.
incidents.impact: Sensitive personal data of thousands of FBI employees exposed including job details, intelligence roles, addresses, and medical records; Jeppesen ForeFlight also extorted; Accenture contractor removed; multiple ShinyHunters members arrested in Jordan, Netherlands, and Pennsylvania.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure, government, healthcare, IT, and law enforcement organizations globally
incidents.vector: Integrity Technology Group, a Chinese government-linked company, employs personnel who provide operational support to malicious actors using AI-automated scanning, large-scale botnets, and manual hands-on exploitation against global targets.
incidents.impact: Ongoing global espionage campaign affecting government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, IT, and law enforcement sectors across Southeast Asia, Africa, and North America; UK previously sanctioned the company; joint advisory co-signed by NSA, FBI, NCSC, and six allied nations.

incidents.victim: Global ransomware victims and cybercrime ecosystem
incidents.vector: Cryptomus (also operating as Certa Payments, Xeltox, and Heleket) processed over $7 billion in cryptocurrency transactions since 2022, providing payment infrastructure for ransomware operators, darknet markets, fraud services, and Russian sanctions evasion.
incidents.impact: UK froze Cryptomus assets and barred British entities from doing business with it; VexPay, TokenSpot, and Tsunami Payments also sanctioned; the platform processed funds for over 900 illicit counterparties in a single recent month.

incidents.victim: Mr. Max Holdings (Japanese discount retailer)
incidents.vector: Unknown attackers gained unauthorized access to MrMax app and online store servers between October 3 and 6, 2026.
incidents.impact: Up to 1,735,154 member records exposed including account IDs, names, email addresses, and phone numbers; credit card data, passwords, and purchase history confirmed not leaked.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
incidents.vector: Three separate threat groups exploited two Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center vulnerabilities for initial access; one group deployed Qilin ransomware and another deployed Cyclops Blink along with credential and configuration theft.
incidents.impact: Multiple victim organizations experienced credential theft, managed-device configuration exfiltration, persistent backdoor implants, and Qilin ransomware deployment across their environments.

incidents.victim: 440+ organizations using PaperCut NG/MF print management software
incidents.vector: Suspected Russian-speaking actor deployed hundreds of AI agents to exploit two PaperCut NG/MF vulnerabilities at machine speed, achieving mass compromise across nearly 400 organizations in a single campaign.
incidents.impact: At least 440 PaperCut instances across 395 organizations compromised; the campaign demonstrated AI-enabled mass exploitation at a scale and speed exceeding traditional human-operated attacks.

incidents.victim: 49+ organizations including critical infrastructure operators
incidents.vector: Exploited vulnerabilities in WordPress, Linux, Gitea, and Proxmox in a coordinated campaign for persistent access, credential collection, and lateral movement across targeted organizations.
incidents.impact: 49+ organizations breached including 11 critical infrastructure entities; source code repositories, databases, and credentials stolen.
